name: TX-37
label: Safe D

model.rationale: The district's roughly 30-point Democratic lean, Casar's ten-to-one fundraising advantage, the absence of any outside spending against him, and markets pricing his win near 98 percent all point to a safe hold; with no public polling available, the precise margin is the main uncertainty.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Casar or unusually depressed Democratic turnout in a low-salience election could narrow the margin, though flipping the seat itself is very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
TX-37 covers much of Austin and is one of the most Democratic-leaning House districts in Texas, with a partisan lean of roughly 30 points toward Democrats. Incumbent Greg Casar is running for reelection, and no outside groups are spending against him. Prediction markets put the Democratic side's chances of holding the seat near 98 percent.

The money gap is stark: Casar has raised about $1.37 million and holds roughly $556,000 on hand, while Republican Lauren Peña has raised about $130,000 and reports just $2,598 in cash. No independent public polls of the general election are available, so expectations rest on the district's strong Democratic fundamentals. In a normal environment, that combination points to a comfortable double-digit win for Casar.
